headword: {立体映像|りったいえいぞう}

definitions.explanation: A visual representation that creates the illusion of depth, appearing to have three dimensions rather than being flat.

examples.japanese: {立体映像|りったいえいぞう}で{映画|えいが}を{楽|たの}しむ。
{最新|さいしん}の{立体映像|りったいえいぞう}{技術|ぎじゅつ}は{眼鏡|めがね}なしで{楽|たの}しめる。
examples.english: The latest 3D imaging technology can be enjoyed without glasses.

examples.japanese: {博物館|はくぶつかん}では{立体映像|りったいえいぞう}を{使|つか}って{恐竜|きょうりゅう}の{時代|じだい}を{再現|さいげん}していた。
examples.english: The museum used 3D images to recreate the age of dinosaurs.

notes:
A compound of {立体|りったい} (three-dimensional; solid) and {映像|えいぞう} (image; video). Used for 3D movies, holograms, VR content, and other visual media that create depth perception. The term covers both still stereoscopic images and moving 3D video.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {立体映像|りったいえいぞう}{技術|ぎじゅつ}: 3D imaging technology
- {立体映像|りったいえいぞう}を{投影|とうえい}する: to project a 3D image
- {立体映像|りったいえいぞう}で{見|み}る: to view in 3D
- {立体映像|りったいえいぞう}コンテンツ: 3D content

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ホログラム: hologram — a specific type of 3D image created by laser interference patterns
- {3D映像|すりーでぃーえいぞう}: 3D video — the loanword-based equivalent, common in casual usage
- {映像|えいぞう}: image; video — the general term for visual media without the 3D element
